verdict.rationale: Token2's own fido2-manage tool documents FIDO2-backed SSH security keys stored on the device. It can generate them, list resident keys, rehydrate them, push them via ssh-copy-id, and load them into ssh-agent, which is the core of the sk-ssh path. PIV is documented only for Windows smartcard and AD logon and macOS login, not for SSH, and nothing in the evidence states that server access requires a physical touch. missing for 10: explicit documentation that SSH authentication requires a physical touch, PIV-based SSH keys, OpenPGP support, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, my SSH keys can be hardware-backed on the device — via FIDO2 sk-ssh keys, PIV, or OpenPGP — so server access requires a physical touch

citations.quote: SSH security keys: generate, list resident, download (rehydrate), upload to a remote (`ssh-copy-id`), add to the local ssh-agent
fido2-manage is a tool allowing to manage FIDO2.1 devices over USB or NFC, including Passkey (resident keys) management
